channel.title: Times of San Diego - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Times of San Diego (timesofsandiego.com)

item.title: 28K pounds of peanut, sunflower seed butters donated to San Diego Food Bank
item.description: San Diego-based nonprofit International Relief Teams has donated 28,776 pounds of peanut and sunflower seed butters to the San Diego Food Bank.

item.title: Opinion: California’s existential issues scare off top candidates for governor
item.description: Could it be that those who dropped out or never dropped in looked at the daunting array of potentially intractable issues they would face?

item.title: Two years lost: Task force simply restated transit agency financial woes it was created to solve
item.description: A task force created to solve a financial cliff facing transit agencies released its report last year, offering few solutions to the problem.

item.title: Beach and Bay Press: Jan. 30, 2026
item.description: The January 30, 2026, Beach & Bay Press cover highlights Pacific Beach news: a new ocean-themed Wildcoast mural by artist Jon Hamrick celebrates 25 years of coastal conservation at 714 Garnet Ave. The Pacific Beach Town Council named Denise Friedman honorary mayor and presented community awards at its 75th annual dinner. Other headlines include a failed vacation rental tax proposal, safer streets calls after a child's tragic death, and local sports/nominations.

item.title: La Jolla Village News: Jan. 30, 2026
item.description: The January 30, 2026, La Jolla Village News features the ongoing harbor seal pupping season at Children's Pool, with beach access restricted through May 15 to protect nursing mothers and pups. Enhance La Jolla advances beautification plans for 2026, including new flower baskets and planters along Girard and Fay Avenues to brighten the Village.

item.title: Dry January leaves California’s vital snowpack well under average
item.description: The second official snow survey of the season found California's snowpack at only 59% of normal, the Department of Water Resources reported.

item.title: La Mesa Courier: Jan. 30, 2026
item.description: This issue of the La Mesa Courier celebrates local youth achievements: Grossmont High varsity cheerleaders qualified for JAMZ Cheer Nationals after strong performances and hard work. 8th grade students from College Prep Middle School (CPMS) led a successful "Stock the Pantry Food Drive," collecting 711 pounds of food for the San Diego Food Bank.

item.title: Seven shows to see in February in San Diego
item.description: While movies seem to be faltering of late, San Diego theater is still going strong. Here are seven shows that might be worth your while, from drama to comedy to musical.

item.title: Hundreds of San Diegans skip work, school for ‘Day of Action’ to protest ICE funding
item.description: Hundreds gathered in San Diego communities and outside high schools to join in ICE protests following violence in Minnesota.

item.title: Actor from GirlsDoPorn going to prison; he’s last defendant sentenced in case
item.description: For years, GirlsDoPorn's owners and operators coerced and tricked hundreds of women into appearing in online pornographic videos.
